skill.name: when-analyzing-user-intent-use-intent-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze ambiguous user requests, rank likely intent, ask targeted questions, and create an execution brief.
skill.summary: Clarifies ambiguous requests before planning or execution.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed real risks around full environment capture, mutable npx-based external tooling, shell script examples, and predictable /tmp output paths. Most static backtick findings were false positives caused by markdown fences or JavaScript template literals, and no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.issue: Full environment capture during intent analysis
remediation.suggestion: Remove process.env from captured context. Collect only needed, nonsecret metadata and redact sensitive values before memory storage.
Pin claude-flow to a reviewed version and require explicit user confirmation before any npx command runs.
Write results to a user-approved workspace path or create a secure temporary directory with restrictive permissions.

remediation.issue: Shell script examples mix file content with external commands
remediation.suggestion: Quote file paths, validate inputs, and pass structured data through files or stdin instead of inline command strings.

static_findings.snippet: header: `I want to make sure I understand your request correctly. Can you clarify:`,
footer: `These clarifications will help me provide exactly what you need.`
summary: `Based on your input, I understand you want to: ${synthesis.understanding}`,
verification: `Does this match your expectations? If not, please let me know what I misunderstood.`
.slice(0, 3); // Max 3 questions to avoid overwhelming user

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Environment and Project Context Capture
semantic_findings.description: The workflow instructs agents to collect process.env, current working directory, filesystem clues, and recent edits for intent analysis. This can collect secrets and sensitive project metadata beyond what intent clarification requires.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented userInput and contextClues objects explicitly include process.env, cwd, filesystem analysis, recent edits, and memory storage. This confirms broad data collection, not just a naming false positive.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable External Tool Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares claude-flow@alpha and repeatedly instructs npx execution. A mutable alpha dependency can change without review and execute third-party code during a clarification workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The dependency and quick start examples explicitly name claude-flow@alpha and npx commands. The supply-chain risk is clear even though many backtick pattern matches were markdown fences.

content.value_statement: Ambiguous requests can lead to incorrect plans, wasted work, and missed constraints. This skill analyzes intent, asks focused questions, and produces a clear execution brief.
actual_capabilities: Breaks a request into actions, subjects, constraints, and desired outcomes.
Ranks multiple interpretations with probability and confidence labels.
Generates up to three clarifying questions for high-impact ambiguities.
Synthesizes a final understanding with scope, approach, deliverables, and risks.
Creates handoff artifacts such as an execution brief and next-step plan.
limitations: Requires user confirmation for uncertain interpretations.
Examples assume claude-flow tooling is available.
May over-collect context unless environment and filesystem access are limited.
Does not execute the final development task by itself.

use_cases.title: Clarify Vague Feature Requests
use_cases.description: Turn a short or unclear feature request into scoped work with assumptions and next steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare Stakeholder Briefs
use_cases.description: Convert rough stakeholder input into a clear execution brief before planning begins.

use_cases.title: Reduce Operational Ambiguity
use_cases.description: Ask focused questions before acting on unclear support, DevOps, or workflow requests.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Simple Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use for a vague task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this request for intent. Identify the likely goal, missing details, and one clarifying question: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Rank Possible Interpretations
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a request has several meanings.
prompt_templates.prompt: List three possible interpretations of this request. Rank them by likelihood and explain the evidence for each one: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Create an Execution Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before handing work to another workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an execution brief from this request. Include interpreted intent, assumptions, constraints, risks, and confirmation questions: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a High-Stakes Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use for sensitive or costly work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a careful intent analysis for this high-stakes request. Limit context to nonsecret data, rank interpretations, and require confirmation before action: [paste request].

output: Likely intent: build a REST API with authentication and authorization.
Clarifying question: which authentication method should be used?
Next step: confirm scope before implementation begins.

output_examples.input: Make the app faster and cleaner.
output: Likely intent: improve performance and simplify visible interface issues.
Ambiguity: faster could mean load time, runtime response, or build speed.
Next step: ask which performance metric matters most.

output_examples.input: Set up deployment for this project.
output: Likely intent: create a repeatable production deployment workflow.
Key assumptions: hosting target, secrets handling, and rollback process are undecided.
Next step: confirm platform and release requirements.

best_practices: Use this skill for ambiguous, complex, or high-impact requests.
Limit context collection and redact secrets before analysis starts.
Confirm the final interpretation before handing work to another workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not run command examples without reviewing dependencies and file paths.
Do not treat a probability score as user consent.
Do not ask more clarifying questions than the decision requires.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a request is vague, multi-part, high-impact, or open to several interpretations.

faq.question: Does it replace user confirmation?
faq.answer: No. It helps form a likely interpretation, but the user should confirm uncertain decisions.

faq.question: Can it create an action plan?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce a concise execution brief with scope, assumptions, risks, and next steps.

faq.question: Does it need access to environment variables?
faq.answer: No. Environment capture should be disabled or redacted unless a user explicitly approves it.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code style workflows.

faq.question: What are the main safety concerns?
faq.answer: Review external command examples, avoid full environment capture, and store outputs in approved paths.
